nodes.name: Nickel Foam Surface Cleaning
nodes.procedure: NF was immersed into ethanol in an ultrasonic cleaner for 5 min to clear contaminants, then ultrasonically cleaned for 2 min with HCl (10 vol%) solution to get rid of the oxide on the NF surface and then rinsed with deionized water for 10 min.

nodes.source_text: Before the electrodeposition, NF was immersed into ethanol in an ultrasonic cleaner for 5 min to clear contaminants, then ultrasonically cleaned for 2 min with HCl (10 vol%) solution to get rid of the oxide on the NF surface and then rinsed with deionized water for 10 min.

nodes.name: One-Step Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A 12-V 10 A power supply instrument was applied for the electrodeposition of MnCoP catalyst on foam Ni (NF). The anode was a graphite sheet, while the cathode was NF. The 40 ml electrolyte solution was composed of 8 mmol·L⁻¹ CoCl₂·6H₂O, 10 mmol·L⁻¹ NaH₂PO₂·H₂O and 8 mmol·L⁻¹ MnSO₄·H₂O. The process of electrodeposition was performed with a current of 0.5 A for each side of NF at 50 °C for 4 min. The loading of the catalyst after drying was 8.85 mg·cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show interwoven MnCoP nanosheets evenly distributed on NF, forming Sepaktakraw-like rattan-like deposits with uniform size of ~250 nm without surface cracks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of MnCoP/NF are displayed in Fig. 2a, b. The interwoven MnCoP nanosheets were evenly distributed on NF, forming a rattan-like deposit with a uniform size (~250 nm) without surface cracks.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows diffraction peaks near 43°, 50° and 75° corresponding to (111), (200) and (220) planes of crystalline Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2d shows XRD pattern of MnCoP/NF. The diffraction peaks near 43°, 50° and 75° correspond to (111), (200) and (220) planes of crystalline Co, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS spectrum shows atomic ratio between Mn and Co of 0.075, consistent with ICP-MS results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on EDS spectrum (Fig. S2), the atomic ratio between Mn and Co was calculated to be 0.075 (Table S1), consistent with the result of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS, Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and elemental mapping confirm homogeneous distribution of Mn, Co, P elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) images in Fig. 2e, f and corresponding elemental mappings of MnCoP catalyst in Fig. 2g further confirmed the homogeneous distribution of Mn, Co, P.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey scan shows Mn 2p, Co 2p, P 2p, O 1s peaks; high-resolution Mn 2p at 653.59 and 642.04 eV (Mn²⁺/Mn³⁺); Co 2p₃/₂ at 781.09 eV (MnCoP) vs 781.44 eV (CoP), Co 2p₁/₂ at 796.94 eV (MnCoP) vs 797.04 eV (CoP); P 2p at ~129 eV (M-P) and ~133 eV (P-O); Mn doping shifts Co-P and P 2p peaks negatively by 0.35 and 0.31 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS from the survey scan of MnCoP collected from NF is shown in Fig. 3a... The Mn 2p peaks at 653.59 and 642.04 eV... could be attributed to Mn 2p₁/₂ and Mn 2p₃/₂... The Co 2p₃/₂ peak 781.09 eV for MnCoP/NF and 781.44 eV for CoP/NF... Compared with CoP/NF, the 2p3/2 peak of Co 2p spectrum and Co-P peak of P 2p spectrum in MnCoP shifted negatively by 0.35 and 0.31 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl of MnCoP/NF is ~15% higher than CoP/NF, calculated from CV in non-Faradaic region at scan rates 4-12 mV/s.
nodes.evidence_snippet: MnCoP/NF possessed ~15% higher value of Cdl than CoP/NF, corresponding to excellent ECSA (Fig. S3c).
